- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days), suggesting a bias toward upward movement.
- Forecasts peak too early after sharp spikes in price (e.g., 79.20–80+), then overshoot and fail to correct — indicating lag in recognizing mean reversion or policy-induced cooling.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits no behavioral adjustment, implying it ignores sentiment as a signal — should incorporate sentiment as a multiplier or offset for volatility.
- In periods with sustained price consolidation (e.g., 74–76 range), model fails to recognize mean reversion and continues trending upward — should apply a decay factor or momentum filter.
- Forecasts for later days (15–30) often underestimate true price, especially after a spike — suggests model overreacts to early momentum and underestimates eventual correction.
- If true outcome shows a sharp reversal (e.g., 85.40 → 80.96), model fails to adjust — should apply a “reversal trigger” rule to reduce forecast slope after 3 consecutive days of high price.
- Model ignores official event context (e.g., policy changes, auction results) — should integrate event-based volatility modifiers into forecast weights.
